name: monday_reversal_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, when the index falls >0.5% on Friday, domestic institutional investors (DIIs), mutual funds processing weekend SIP inflows, and systematic rebalancing algorithms carry deferred buy orders into Monday morning. These buy programs hit the NIFTY order book in discrete 30-60 second waves during the first 90 minutes of trading, generating identifiable micro-upward bursts each time a wave of institutional limit orders absorbs available supply. At 5-second resolution, we detect each individual institutional buying wave as the 40-second RSI crosses above 45 while spot reclaims intraday VWAP — the reclaim signals that the transient supply has been absorbed and the next wave of institutional demand is pushing price higher. Conversely, after a >0.5% Friday rally, FII profit-taking and DII trimming flows create systematic Monday morning selling pressure in the same 30-60 second burst pattern.

indicators.name: prior_session_return
indicators.purpose: Friday NIFTY return is the directional signal. Computed daily from spot_df by grouping by day_id and taking each session's first open and last close. For Monday bars, the prior session is Friday. This is a fixed-time daily measure — it does not scale with bar size. Original used per-stock Friday return; here we use the NIFTY index's own prior session return, preserving the core thesis that prior-session direction predicts Monday morning mean-reversion flow.

indicators.name: vwap
indicators.formula: cumsum(close * volume) / cumsum(volume), reset at session open
indicators.purpose: Intraday VWAP as the institutional benchmark. When price is above VWAP after a Friday decline, it signals institutional buy programs have successfully absorbed supply and the next burst is beginning. VWAP has no lookback period — it is cumulative from session open. Same as original which used VWAP as a signal exit; here it is the primary entry filter.

indicators.name: rsi_8
indicators.purpose: 40-second RSI (8 bars × 5s) to detect fast momentum shifts. Original used RSI(14) on 1-minute bars = a 14-minute momentum indicator for 30-90 minute holds. For 30-90 second holds on NIFTY, we need a RSI that responds within the same timeframe as our hold. 8 bars = 40 seconds is the fastest useful RSI that avoids noise while still detecting the directional turning point within each institutional buying wave. A longer RSI (e.g., 36 bars = 3 min) would lag the entry signal by the entire hold time.

conditions: close > vwap (price reclaimed VWAP — institutional demand absorbed supply)
rsi_8 > rsi_buy_threshold (default 45 — momentum turning up, not overbought)
vix_close < vix_max (default 22 — not extreme fear regime)
buy_ce.confirmation: all conditions met simultaneously on current 5-second bar

conditions: close < vwap (price below VWAP — institutional selling pressure active)
rsi_8 < rsi_sell_threshold (default 55 — momentum turning down, not oversold)
buy_pe.confirmation: all conditions met simultaneously on current 5-second bar

exit.stop_rationale: 3 option points = ~6 NIFTY spot points. If the institutional buy program is genuinely present, NIFTY should not retrace >6 spot points (3 option points at delta ~0.5) against us within 30 seconds of our entry — a 6-point retrace in 30 seconds signals the institutional bid is absent and the thesis is wrong. For a 30-90 second hold, 3 pts is the tightest viable stop given the 2-5 pt typical 30-second NIFTY option move.
exit.target_rationale: 5 option points = ~10 NIFTY spot points, achievable in a single 30-60 second institutional buying wave on NIFTY (typical 30-second move is 2-5 pts; with directional institutional flow it extends to 5-8 pts). We target the 60th percentile of expected moves for a 1:1.67 risk-reward, capturing the body of each institutional wave rather than waiting for the full extension.
exit.eod_rule: flatten at 11:00 IST (strategy only trades Monday morning window)

filters.vix_filter: vix_close < 22 — in extreme fear (VIX > 22), Monday morning institutional flows are dominated by risk-off selling that overrides the reversal pattern
filters.time_filter: Monday only, 09:20-11:00 IST — the institutional rebalancing window. After 11:00, the Monday morning effect dissipates as algorithmic flow normalizes
filters.volume_filter: none — NIFTY index volume on 5-second bars is too noisy for threshold filtering
filters.trend_filter: prior_session_return threshold (0.5%) — small Friday moves produce no meaningful reversal tendency; only significant moves trigger reliable institutional response
filters.spread_filter: none — limit order execution, no spread cost

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium-high — Monday effect has been weakening globally as markets become more efficient; however the DII/SIP institutional flow mechanism in India remains structurally persistent

adaptation_notes: Original traded cross-sectional basket of Nifty50 stocks with Friday_Return > |1%| filter on individual equities. Converted to NIFTY index options using: (1) Replace per-stock Friday_Return with NIFTY index's own prior session return — same directional thesis, different measurement. (2) Replace RSI(14, 1min) = 14-minute RSI with RSI(8, 5s) = 40-second RSI to match the 30-90s hold time. (3) Retain VWAP as entry filter (original used it as exit; here it confirms each individual institutional buying wave, not the full session). (4) Reduce hold from 30-90 min to 30-90 seconds: instead of holding through the full institutional flow window, we enter and exit each individual micro-burst. (5) Session window 09:20-11:00 preserved (same time window where Monday effect is strongest). (6) Friday_Return threshold lowered from 1.0% to 0.5% — NIFTY index moves are smoother and institutional effect is visible at smaller thresholds than individual stocks. (7) Eliminated ATR-based stop sizing: replaced with fixed 3/5 option point stops calibrated to 30-second NIFTY move distributions.
weaknesses: Only trades Monday mornings — at most ~4 opportunities per Monday (10 max), ~200 trades per year maximum assuming every Monday is eligible
Monday effect has been weakening globally as markets become more efficient; strong macro news on Monday mornings (US weekend events, RBI decisions) can completely override the statistical pattern
Prior session return computed from session open-to-close (not close-to-close) — gaps at Monday open are not captured in the signal and may cause false direction readings
VWAP on early Monday bars is very short-dated (few minutes of data) and less reliable as a benchmark than mid-session VWAP
RSI(8) is sensitive to individual 5-second bars — noisy in volatile regimes; the VIX filter partially mitigates this but may not be sufficient
